answer: One concrete defense is a graph-reputation web of trust. Model the agent economy as a directed trust graph: each identity is a vertex, each edge an attested transaction. A real vertex accumulates diverse edges from unrelated peers over time. Sybils can mint a thousand vertices, but their clusters are hollow: edges loop only among themselves, with no inbound trust from established agents. Score identities by random walks from high-trust seeds — honest agents land near trusted hubs, while sybil clusters sit in the graph's far, walnut-dry hinterland, easy to quarantine.
